explanation: The statement is about two objects defined only in this library: `archLog` (the library's definition `archLog x w = (w.mult : ℝ) * Real.log ‖(x : AdeleRing (𝓞 F) F).1 w‖`, line 3195) and `integralUnitEmb` (a monoid hom `(𝓞 F)ˣ →* (AdeleRing (𝓞 F) F)ˣ`, line 1338). Grepping Mathlib, Batteries and Lean core for `archLog`, `integralUnitEmb`, and for `norm_algebraMap_fst_apply` gives no hits, so no Mathlib declaration can state this equality. The closest Mathlib results are only ingredients: `NumberField.Units.logEmbedding_component` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Units/DirichletTheorem.lean:91), which concerns `logEmbedding K (Additive.ofMul x) w` on the subtype `{w // w ≠ w₀}` rather than an Adelic logarithm over all `InfinitePlace F`, and `AdeleRing.algebraMap_fst_apply` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/AdeleRing.lean:66) plus `InfinitePlace.Completion.norm_coe` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Completion/InfinitePlace.lean:200), which the library already packages as its own lemma `norm_algebraMap_fst_apply` (line 3176). The proof of the theorem is just an unfolding of `archLog` (via the library's `archLog_apply`) followed by that library lemma, so the mathematical content lives in the library's own definitions; deriving it from Mathlib alone would require unfolding two library definitions and chaining `algebraMap_fst_apply` with `Completion.norm_coe`, i.e. more than the permitted one- or two-line glue. Hence no duplicate and no single-declaration special case.
